objective: Reduce moving-frame latency versus the rebased exact-LOD renderer without losing more than 0.5 dB minimum foreground PSNR or worsening p95 by over 20 percent; compare the result to stock upstream main on larger inputs

ideas.title: PC contribution cutoff
ideas.claim: Cull low integrated-opacity Gaussians before sort and raster.

provenance.evidence: PC defaults use contribution=3 and are faster than our unfiltered LOD on both object scenes, but the combined-default comparison does not isolate this mechanism.
provenance.boundary: Same Apple GPU, input and viewport; approximation needs an error check.

ideas.title: PC footprint cutoff
ideas.claim: Dropping sub-two-pixel Gaussians reduces sort and raster work.

provenance.evidence: Stock minPixelSize=2; prior bee default PSNR of 18.04 dB is a warning that aggressive default filters may be unsuitable.
provenance.boundary: Can discard substantial aggregate opacity; never assume an invisible loss.

ideas.title: PC cached SH
ideas.claim: Reuse work-buffer SH until the camera-direction change justifies refreshing it.

provenance.evidence: Native PC uses a 10-degree update threshold; our existing visible-only path deliberately bypasses that cache.
provenance.boundary: Full-bank color refreshes can cost more than visible-only SH in large scenes.

ideas.title: Selected-ID SH cache
ideas.claim: Cache directional color only for selected visible permanent IDs and refresh changed directions incrementally.

provenance.evidence: Whole-bank cached SH has worse shop tails than visible-only evaluation. A smaller cache is not yet tested.
provenance.boundary: SH3 inputs; exact ID and per-splat direction validity must survive LOD and camera changes.

ideas.title: Coverage-preserving tiny-splat aggregation
ideas.claim: Replace groups of weak subpixel splats with screen-space representatives instead of discarding their opacity.

provenance.evidence: Contribution culling loses 9.6 dB on bee and 4 dB on 32M city despite speed gains. Preserving aggregate coverage may repair the failure.
provenance.boundary: Approximate; differing depth and SH prohibit indiscriminate pixel-bin merges.

ideas.title: One-time physical bank locality
ideas.claim: Order each immutable bank spatially while retaining a permanent logical-to-physical ID map.

provenance.evidence: All bank parameters remain resident and large-source traversal costs persist. Cache-local memory access is an untested orthogonal direction.
provenance.boundary: Must not enable loader reorder without updating ID maps, metadata digests and SH addressing.

components.claim: Use integrated projected opacity, not distance alone, to reject a Gaussian.
Use PC's existing contribution cutoff of 3 in the projector.
Use the Gaussian's projected footprint to reject small splats.
Use PC's two-pixel footprint cutoff in addition to contribution culling.
Evaluate visible SH after fine culling on every current view.
Use native PC work-buffer color updates at a ten-degree threshold.
Reject a new default if minimum foreground PSNR falls by over 0.5 dB or p95 increases by over 20 percent against exact LOD.
Store cached color keyed by permanent selected Gaussian ID.
Refresh only newly visible or direction-invalid cached colors.
Use per-splat view direction change, including translation, to invalidate color.
Moment-merge compatible tiny projected splats while preserving opacity rather than hard-culling them.
Restrict projected aggregation to bounded depth and color variation.
Estimate aggregate projected coverage of weak splats before replacing a group.
Use physically spatially ordered immutable parameter banks.
Preserve logical world IDs with a one-time bijective address remap.
Compare same-selected-ID renders and frame tails before considering locality a win.

proposals.title: Contribution culling with current-view visible SH
proposals.hypothesis: Contribution=3 removes costly low-opacity splats without materially reducing the existing LOD quality.
proposals.mechanism: Set minContribution=3, retain minPixelSize=0, then evaluate SH only for surviving projected splats.
proposals.interaction: The fine cull saves both SH work and later sorting/raster work; it does not add a full-bank color refresh.
proposals.baseline: Rebased exact LOD 2x: zero cutoffs, visible SH
proposals.test: Bee and shop, 2560x1440, 2 reversed trials; validate frozen settings on 16.18M and 32.37M Lublin inputs
proposals.primary_metric: Pooled median completed moving-frame latency, separately per scene
guardrails: Minimum foreground PSNR no more than 0.5 dB below exact LOD
Moving p95 no more than 20 percent worse
Same input count, SH terms, paths, resolution and GPU sort
proposals.rejection_rule: Do not promote as a default without at least 5 percent median gain and both quality and tail guards passing on selection and larger tests.
failure_modes: Many individually weak splats jointly cover an opaque surface
proposals.cost: One bounded local batch; no paid services; under 100 GB of derived artifacts
proposals.boundary: Single Apple M5 Max device and fixed paths

score_reasons.evidence_strength: Default bundle was faster but unisolated.
score_reasons.expected_impact: Saves work before SH, sorting and draw.

proposals.title: PC fine culling plus visible SH
proposals.hypothesis: PC's additional two-pixel cutoff accelerates LOD while retaining its measured quality.
proposals.mechanism: Set minPixelSize=2 and minContribution=3 with the existing visible-only SH projector.
proposals.interaction: Footprint and opacity signals reject different splats; evaluating SH after both avoids paying for discarded colors.
proposals.baseline: Rebased exact LOD 2x; also compare P1 to isolate footprint cutoff
proposals.test: Same frozen paired bee/shop and larger-city protocol as P1
proposals.primary_metric: Pooled median completed moving-frame latency, separately per scene
guardrails: Minimum foreground PSNR within 0.5 dB of exact LOD
Moving p95 within 20 percent of exact LOD
proposals.rejection_rule: Promote only with at least 5 percent median gain and all guards passing; retain failed-quality settings only as explicit opt-in.
failure_modes: Two-pixel cutoff can erase dense fur or thin details, as suggested by prior bee default error
proposals.boundary: Fixed full-resolution views on one device

score_reasons.evidence_strength: Prior default comparison exposed both speed and quality differences.
score_reasons.information_gain: Tests whether default footprint policy fits merged splats.

proposals.title: PC culling and cached SH
proposals.hypothesis: Reusing PC's color work buffer is cheaper than evaluating visible SH every moving frame.
proposals.mechanism: Use PC-default fine culling, disable fused visible SH, and keep PC colorUpdateAngle=10 with native work-buffer updates.
proposals.interaction: Culling cuts raster work while cached color avoids repeated SH when the camera remains inside the update cone.
proposals.baseline: P2 isolates SH schedule; exact LOD remains the quality guard
proposals.test: Same protocol, including full camera translation and rotation; SH0 city inputs cannot establish an SH-reuse benefit
proposals.primary_metric: Pooled median completed moving-frame latency, separately per scene
guardrails: Foreground PSNR within 0.5 dB of exact LOD
Moving p95 within 20 percent of exact LOD
Fresh globally sorted geometry every frame
proposals.rejection_rule: Do not promote if color refresh spikes erase median gains or either quality guard fails.
failure_modes: Full resident-bank color updates cost more than visible-only SH
proposals.cost: Same bounded local batch; no extra color buffers
proposals.boundary: Native PC whole-bank caching may be unsuitable inside large chunks

score_reasons.evidence_strength: Mechanism available but not independently tested in our renderer.
score_reasons.information_gain: Resolves whether our visible-SH choice was useful.

proposals.title: Visible-ID color cache with projected-error validation
proposals.hypothesis: A per-selected-ID SH cache lowers moving latency without the whole-bank refresh spikes seen in P3.
proposals.mechanism: Allocate a color and last-direction entry by permanent world ID; during projection evaluate SH for first-use or direction-invalid entries and reuse others. Use projected footprint and a measured SH error bound to require tighter validity for more visible splats. Keep source SH and full-quality geometry.
proposals.interaction: Permanent IDs allow view-to-view reuse while the footprint signal prevents treating a large close-up splat like a subpixel one. The existing quality and p95 guard rejects stale color.
proposals.baseline: Current exact LOD plus visible SH; separately compare native cached SH
proposals.test: Prototype and audit on synthetic SH3, then frozen bee/shop paths with stationary, rotation, translation and LOD-change cases
proposals.primary_metric: Moving completed-frame median with cold-refresh and steady-state costs reported separately
guardrails: At most 0.5 dB loss versus current LOD
No stale ID aliasing or hidden coefficient reduction
proposals.rejection_rule: Reject if cold-refresh spikes erase gains or the error guard fails; do not extrapolate SH0 results.
failure_modes: Cache memory and random writes exceed saved SH cost
Directional error bound is too loose
proposals.cost: One new GPU cache and projection branch; requires a separate authorized experiment batch
proposals.boundary: Static SH3 scenes, one device until replicated

score_reasons.evidence_strength: P3 identifies refresh tails, not this solution's benefit.
score_reasons.expected_impact: May save visible SH without full-bank updates.
score_reasons.feasibility: Permanent IDs and projection hooks already exist.
score_reasons.information_gain: Separates cache granularity from cache validity.

proposals.title: Locality-assisted, coverage-preserving projected aggregation
proposals.hypothesis: Aggregating compatible tiny splats instead of discarding them retains aggregate opacity while reducing sort and raster work.
proposals.mechanism: Spatially order immutable banks with a permanent ID remap, bin projected tiny splats locally, and moment-merge only groups with bounded depth and color variation. Preserve summed optical contribution and depth-order constraints; leave incompatible splats unchanged. Compare locality-only, aggregation-only and combined controls.
proposals.interaction: Physical locality can reduce binning and parameter-gather cost, while depth/color constraints prevent locality from merging unrelated overlapping surfaces. This directly addresses P1's lost aggregate coverage.
prerequisites: Stable output IDs and global sorting
proposals.baseline: Exact LOD with visible SH, plus P1 contribution cutoff as a loss-control
proposals.test: Synthetic overlapping-opacity/depth-edge scenes followed by the same frozen bee, shop and city paths; retain the three ablations
proposals.primary_metric: Total moving completed-frame latency including binning and reduction
guardrails: At most 0.5 dB additional minimum foreground PSNR loss
Bijection of logical IDs after physical reordering
proposals.rejection_rule: Reject if binning/reduction costs more than the saved work or opacity/depth guard fails.
failure_modes: No compatible groups at fine depth edges
SH and internal occlusion do not merge well
Physical reordering alone changes tie order
proposals.cost: Substantial new compute path; untested and outside the completed three-proposal budget
proposals.boundary: Projected subpixel groups only; not a license to merge all distant geometry

score_reasons.evidence_strength: Cutoff failure establishes the coverage problem, not this solution.
score_reasons.expected_impact: Can reduce sort and raster while retaining coverage.
score_reasons.feasibility: WebGPU reductions exist but depth-safe grouping is nontrivial.
score_reasons.testability: Three explicit ablations and synthetic opacity controls.
score_reasons.information_gain: Distinguishes locality cost from aggregation quality.
score_reasons.generality: SH0 and SH3, subject to compatibility.
score_reasons.novelty: New projected aggregation operator and bank layout.
score_reasons.cost_efficiency: Extra passes could erase all gains.

rejections.reason: Same implementation as P2; no separate mechanism or independent test needed.
Contribution-only plus cached SH is deferred to keep this adoption batch at three experiments; P3 tests stock cached SH after stock culling.
Same fine-culling and visible-SH implementation as P2.
Physical bank order and directional cache invalidation have no direct causal interaction without a cache operator. Test locality alone as an ablation in P5 rather than invent a combined win.
Footprint plus depth/color constraints and visible SH identifies eligible groups but supplies no reduction operator. The complete aggregation operator is covered by P5.
Aggregate coverage does not determine directional SH-cache validity. Coupling the signals could reuse stale color.
Depth/color constraints and existing visible SH plus a quality guard are not a new acceleration operator.

protocol.baseline: Stock upstream main d753e98c70d67b755754c614f383d215cacbbd63, release/minified build; exact LOD on the same base is the optimization control
protocol.selection_data: Frozen Bee and Ekotori full scans and paths from packages/splat-lod/benchmark/scenes.mjs
protocol.holdout_policy: Freeze all three stock-setting candidates and guards before reading large-city timing or image-error results. Camera/setup preflights are not selection evidence. Report every variant, including regressions.
protocol.primary_metric: Median completed moving-frame latency pooled across two reversed-order trials, separately per scene
guardrails: 0.5 dB maximum reduction in minimum foreground PSNR from exact LOD
20 percent maximum moving p95 regression from exact LOD
All available source SH, global current-view GPU sorting, identical physical 2560x1440 resolution
protocol.promotion_rule: A default needs at least 5 percent moving-median improvement with both guards passing in selection and larger-input validation. Otherwise keep exact as default and expose useful lossy profiles explicitly.
protocol.failure_handling: Retain failures and errors; no best-run picking. One fresh closed browser tab per case. Incomplete or hidden-tab measurements are invalid, not slow-renderer results. If rerunning a scene after setup repair, rerun all of its modes in prescribed order.
protocol.budget: One three-proposal selection batch, then the same fixed variants on two larger inputs; 7 configurations x 4 inputs x 2 trials, 90 static and 90 moving frames each. Under 100 GB disk, no paid services. Stop after reporting that batch; record but do not automatically execute a fresh next frontier.

learnings.claim: Contribution culling buys speed but aggregate low-opacity detail makes a universal cutoff unsafe.
learnings.evidence: P1 moving reductions: 31.7% bee, 5.7% shop, 5.5% 16M and 11.9% 32M. Minimum foreground PSNR losses: 9.555, 0.039, 0.351 and 4.034 dB respectively.
learnings.implication: Keep cutoff opt-in; preserve total projected coverage if replacing it with a new reduction operator.

learnings.claim: A two-pixel cutoff after contribution culling did not add a consistent speed benefit.
learnings.evidence: P2 has nearly the same minimum PSNR as P1 but is slower at the pooled moving median on all four inputs; two trials do not establish a small timing difference as causal.
learnings.implication: Do not stack additional cutoffs merely because they are defaults.

learnings.claim: Native whole-bank cached SH did not dominate current-view visible SH.
learnings.evidence: Shop p95 14.54 ms cached versus 8.19 ms with the same culling and visible SH; SH0 city data cannot establish SH reuse benefit.
learnings.implication: Any new SH cache should avoid whole-bank refresh spikes and remain current enough on translated views.
